text:
Shanice: Heads-up — support asked for an automatic model-variant fallback when primary model is saturated. They want it by customer tier + region. Can we discuss constraints?
Ben: +1 on product ask. Clarify: fallback should be capacity-based (GPU queue length / token throttling) not just error rate, right?
Priya: Yes — capacity-based. We had spikes yesterday where requests queued 30s and returned 429s. Fallback would route to a compatible smaller/quantized variant in a different capacity pool in the same region or next-best region for premium customers.
Miguel: Important: SLOs by tier. Premium customers require <100ms token latency ideally — fallback should prefer same-region higher-cost burst before cross-region. Standard/free can go to cross-region cheaper variants.
Shanice: Agree. Proposed rules: 1) if queue depth > X or pending token wait > Y, try same-region compatible variants in order of fidelity. 2) Only cross-region as last resort for non-SLA tiers. 3) Respect data residency flag — never cross-region if customer pinned to region.
Ben: How do we detect "compatible"? Model family + tokenizer compatibility. We should maintain a model compatibility matrix in the routing service. Samples: gpt-3.5-family -> gpt-3.5-quant, gpt-4 -> gpt-4-lite, etc.
Priya: Also need quality fencing: if a fallback reduces expected generation quality by >Z% (per eval metric) and customer is on an enterprise plan under accuracy SLA, we should not fallback — instead queue or alert.
Tom: Implementation note: routing service needs an async probe to check variant readiness and load. Suggest exposing a small health/load endpoint on pool managers returning queue_len, avg_token_latency, free_gpus.
DevOps Bot: deploy: routing-v2 can be staged to canary 5% on eng-platform for testing. Use config flag `enable_capacity_fallback` and per-customer policy overrides.
Miguel: Telemetry plan: emit events for every fallback with tags: customer_id, tier, original_model, chosen_variant, reason (queue_depth/latency/capacity), region_from/to, estimated_quality_delta. We should surface a per-customer dashboard in Console showing fallback rate and top variants.
Ben: Quotas interplay: if customer max_qps or reserved tokens prevent routing to variant (billing footprint / reserved capacity), fallback should consider billing constraints. For dedicated customers, fallback within their reserved pools only.
Priya: UX for Console: show a toggle per deployment: Auto-fallback (Off/Conservative/Aggressive), where Conservative only uses same-region near-equivalent variants, Aggressive can cross-region and quantized variants. Also expose a "preview impact" button that runs sims on recent traffic.
Shanice: Good. Who owns the compatibility matrix and the Console UI? I can take matrix + routing logic. Priya take Console and telemetry. Ben help on API semantics and quota checks. Miguel will add pool health API. Tom helps canary rollout.
Ben: API semantics: POST /v1/route should still return model_id chosen; add field `fallback_chain` array explaining candidates tried. For streaming, include header `x-redwood-fallback: true` if we fell back after starting. Need to be careful with partial responses.
Miguel: Edge case: what if fallback triggers mid-stream because cache/PROMPT->KV cache mismatch? We should avoid switching model mid-request. Instead, if model becomes saturated during an active request, let it finish or return a graceful 503 with reason.
Priya: Tests: unit for routing rules, integration sim with SLO-breach traffic, e2e to validate Console toggle. Also add automated regression eval that measures quality delta for fallbacks on held-out prompts.
Tom: Rollout plan: feature-flagged, canary 5% internal -> 10% dev tenants -> 25% opt-in customers -> full. Metrics to watch: fallback_rate, success_rate, latency_p50/p95, quality_regression_rate.
Shanice: Also add audit log entry whenever we fallback for enterprise customers (for legal/compliance).
Ben: One more: make sure billing attribution is correct. If a cross-region variant costs more, charge accordingly and show cost delta in Console for customer.
Priya: I'll draft a Console mockup and a short README for product/legal.
Shanice: Cool. Action items: Shanice implement compatibility matrix PR, Miguel add health endpoint + docs, Ben update routing API + quota checks, Priya Console + telemetry, Tom rollout plan + canary config. I'll open tracking ticket.
Miguel: Quick question — what thresholds X/Y? Suggest queue_depth > 50 or pending_token_wait > 2000ms as starting point for standard tier. We can tune.
Ben: Agree. Let's start conservative.
Shanice: Thanks team — I'll drop the ticket with proposed thresholds and link to this thread. :thumbsup:
DevOps Bot: Created ticket INF-4123: "Auto model variant fallback - capacity-based" assigned to Shanice, due 2025-04-04.
